# dsh-telegram-notify

One-way Telegram notifications for DeepSeek Harness.
When you are away from the DSH UI, the bot tell

s you that a turn finished,
failed, is waiting for an answer, has a plan ready for review, or needs

a tool
approval. It never reads Telegram updates, so the bot stays send-only.

The plugin ships its own **Settings → Telegram** page: paste the bot token,
enter the chat id, and p
ick which events notify you. No YAML editing needed.
## Events
| Event | Message | Toggle |

| A turn completes | ✅ Turn complete | `notifyTurnComplete` |
| A turn fails, is blocked, or hits th

e token limit | ❌ / ⚠️ | `notifyTurnError` |
| A turn is cancelled | ⏹ Turn cancelled | `notifyTurnA

borted` (off by default) |
| `ask_user_question` waits for an answer | ❓ Waiting for your input | `n

otifyQuestions` |
| A plan is presented for approval (`exit_plan_mode` / plan-review question) | 📋 P

lan ready for approval | `notifyPlanReviews` |
| A tool approval waits for a human | 🔐 Approval need
ed | `notifyApprovals` |

Subagent sessions are ignored. Approval and question notifications wait 400 ms
and are cancelled if

the corresponding decision/tool result arrives first, so
instantly rejected approvals and instantly
failing tool calls stay quiet.

Messages are fire-and-forget. A Telegram outage is logged as a warning and
never fails, blocks, or d
elays an agent turn.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

If your app runs the `desktop` profile, use `--profile desktop`. From a local
checkout (before the n
pm release), use `dsh plugin --profile web add link:$PWD`.

Enable the bundle by adding `"dsh-telegram-notify"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in
`~/.dsh/profiles/web

/package.json` (or enable it from the DSH Plugin Manager).
The bundle patch mounts the `telegram-not

json` (or enable it from the DSH Plugin Manager).
The bundle patch mounts the `telegram-notify` row.
Restart DSH, open **Settings → Telegram**, and:

1. Paste the bot token and press **Save token**. It is stored in the DSH
credential store under the

reference shown on the page
(`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` by default), never in the plugin configuration.
2.

Enter the chat id and press **Save settings**.
3. Pick the events you want and save again.
### Getting a bot and chat id

Create a bot with @BotFather and copy its token.
Send the bot a message first, then ask a helper bot

negative id (for example
`-1001234567890`); `@channelusername` also works for public channels.

The plugin only calls `sendMessage`. It never calls `getUpdates`, so it cannot
consume messages mean
t for another Telegram integration.
## Configuration reference

The Settings page writes the profile patch for the `telegram-notify` row. The
same fields remain edi
table in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `chatId` | `""` (disabled) | Target chat id, or `@channelusername`. |
| `tokenRef` | `TELEGRAM_BOT

_TOKEN` | Credential reference holding the bot token. |
| `token` | unset | Literal token for headle

ss/one-off runs. The Settings page never writes this; prefer `tokenRef`. |
| `apiBase` | `https://ap

i.telegram.org` | Bot API base URL; only change for a local Bot API server. |
| `silent` | `false` |

Send without a notification sound. |
| `notifyTurnComplete` | `true` | Completed turns. |
| `notify

TurnError` | `true` | Failed, blocked, and max-token turns. |
| `notifyTurnAborted` | `false` | Canc

elled turns. |
| `notifyQuestions` | `true` | Pending user questions. |
| `notifyPlanReviews` | `tru

e` | Plans waiting for approval. |
| `notifyApprovals` | `true` | Pending tool approvals. |

The Settings page is keyed to the loader row id `telegram-notify`; mounting the
plugin under a diffe

rent id makes the page report the namespace as unavailable.
The editable page fields are schemastery

`volatile` config, so saves apply to
the running plugin without a restart. Messages are plain text

(no parse mode),
so model output cannot break formatting or inject markup; text is clipped to
Telegr
am's 4096-character limit.

If you also run a two-way Telegram bridge such as `dsh-im`, sessions handled by
that bridge produce

their own replies, and this plugin will additionally send
turn notifications for them. Disable the b

ridge or turn off the turn toggles
if that is noisy.
## How it works

The Host half subscribes to `session/event`. It formats messages from
`turn/end`, `tool/call` (`ask_

user_question`, `exit_plan_mode`),
`approval/asked`/`approval/decided`, `assistant/message`, `user/m

essage`, and
`session/title`, and posts them with `fetch`. The browser half registers a
`settings.se

ction` slot and reads/writes the `telegram-notify` namespace through
`ctx.configForms`; the token go

es through the credentials remote. The Host
plugin disables the auto-generated config form so the se

cret `token` field is
never exposed by a generic page.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Source layout: `src/index.ts` (Host), `src/client.ts` (browser settings page,
compiled as a classic

module-loader script), `test/` (Host event pipeline,
client registration, and server-rendered settin

gs page). No test touches
Telegram; the transport tests use a local HTTP stub.

The first npm publish must authenticate with a token (trusted publishing can
only be configured afte
r the package exists):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then add this repository as a trusted publisher for `dsh-telegram-notify` on
npm (package settings →

Trusted publishing → GitHub Actions, workflow
`publish.yml`). Subsequent releases publish through O

IDC from
`.github/workflows/publish.yml` when a GitHub release is published.
